summary.intent: Continue finishing the post-merge work on the caliper repo: ship the heap-meter wrap fix and the private-member-name fix, then reorganize the oversized trail 405 into smaller focused trails and keep working.
summary.outcome: Heap-meter fix passed its gates and was committed and pushed (linked to trail 405). Four new trails (468–471) were created. The private-name fix was implemented and verified on react-spectrum (all 767 differences were the intended rename), passed lint and workspace tests, and was committed; it has not yet been pushed or linked to Determinism (469).

repo: Work happens in per-fix git worktrees under .claude/worktrees/, each needing its own JS dependency install.
Changes ship with a lint gate that checks the changeset format; the repo formatter must be run on the .changeset/*.md file before the gate passes.
A change (branch) can belong to only one trail, so the heap-meter branch cannot be moved from trail 405 to Determinism after being linked.
Spectrum output stores interned ids and content hashes of prop entries, so a field rename changes hashes; comparing before/after requires expanding the interned tables to see real differences.
A previously built release binary can predate recent merges (#509/#510), so a fair main-vs-fix comparison needs a main-equivalent build, achieved by temporarily disabling the strip.

code.finding: property_name now strips private-member decoration, so `__#N@#type` becomes `#type`. The unit test fails when the strip is disabled, confirming it exercises the fix.

workflow: Verify a fix with a mutation check: disable the change and confirm the new test fails.
For output-affecting changes, build a true baseline binary from the same tree with the fix disabled and classify every diff (hash swap vs intended change) rather than eyeballing it.
Ask for confirmation before creating or reorganizing trails; the assistant proposed the plan and waited for a go.
Cap trails at about 8 changes or one outcome to keep them manageable.

friction: The first lint gate run failed for a real reason that required reading the log head and running the formatter.
The initial before/after spectrum comparison was invalid because the saved binary predated #509/#510, forcing a rebuild with the strip disabled.
Even against a true main build the output differed due to content hashes, requiring extra scripts (pncheck.py, pndiff.py) to expand interned ids and classify diffs.
Attempting to link the heap-meter branch to Determinism failed because a change belongs to a single trail.
